Seasonal profile: one line per year

Source: R/plots.R
op_plot_seasonal.Rd

Plots month of the year on the x-axis and one line per calendar year, with earlier years in graduated grey and the most recent year in colour, so seasonality (for example the winter peak in antibiotic prescribing) and year-to-year change are visible together.

Usage

op_plot_seasonal(
  data,
  y = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  date = "date",
  years = NULL,
  highlight_year = NULL,
  label_years = TRUE,
  facet_scales = c("free_y", "fixed"),
  ylab = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  source = TRUE,
  base_size = 8
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with a date column and a numeric column to plot.

y

Column to plot. Default "rate" if present, otherwise "items".

facet

Column to split into small multiples, usually the antimicrobial ("ab_name", used automatically if present with several values). The data must hold one series per facet and month; filter to a single organisation first.

date

Date column (default "date").

years

Optional integer vector of years to show (default: all).

highlight_year

Year drawn in colour (default: the latest year).

label_years

Label lines with the year at their right-hand end (default TRUE).

facet_scales

Scales for facets: "free_y" (default) or "fixed".

ylab, title, subtitle

Text. title should state the finding in a sentence; it is NULL by default (put the message in the figure caption of your paper).

source

Add the data-source caption (default TRUE); or a custom character string.

base_size

Base font size (default 8 pt, see theme_op()).

Value

A ggplot2::ggplot() object.

Examples

ex <- op_example[op_example$ab_name %in% c("Amoxicillin", "Nitrofurantoin"), ]
op_plot_seasonal(ex, y = "items", years = 2022:2026)
